Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

reasonable adjective

fair, sensible

also fair, it’s only fair, unreasonable, within reason, sensible (of a request)

classical

Traupman 152: fair, fair-minded
Ter. Eun. 3.2.25: quae līberum scīre aequom est adulēscentem (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Imp. Pomp. 47: sīcut aequum est

aequus, aequa, aequum

adjective; aequum est + accusative and infinitive, it is reasonable

fair, reasonable, right

First “level, even”; so fair, just, reasonable. Aequī bonīque facere is “to accept as fair, put up with” (Ter. Heaut. 4.5.40). More than is reasonable is plūs aequō (Hor. Ep. 2.2.215: pōtus largius aequō).

Other words

  • ratiōnī cōnsentāneus — in keeping with reason, reasonable

    phrase: cōnsentāneus with the dative · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 3.20: ratiōnī disciplīnaeque maximē cōnsentānea (Lewis & Short, s.v. cōnsentāneus); M-O s.v. reasonable

    Of an opinion or an argument rather than a person; cōnsentāneum est, “it stands to reason”.

Examples

  • pōtus largius aequō

    having drunk more than is reasonableHor. Ep. 2.2.215 (Lewis & Short)

  • Aequum est tē quoque aliquid labōris suscipere.

    It’s only fair that you take on some of the work too.composed

See also medium, sense, consistent.
